short_title: Rosetta/Mars Express FDS-MCS Interface Control Document
organisation: ESA/ESOC; prepared by Anite Systems GmbH

summary:
The interface control document between the Rosetta and Mars Express mission control systems (RMCS/MEMCS, both [SCOS-2000](../scos2000/index.md) based and developed by Anite) and the ESOC Flight Dynamics System (FDS) on the ORATOS platforms. It lists every data flow in both directions, explains how each one travels, and records the MIB tailoring these missions used.

From the MCS to the FDS go [MIB](../mib/index.md) files, packetised data and tracking data files. The packetised data are TM source packets, TC history and time coefficient packets, which flight dynamics extracts from the MCS data archive with its own SCOS-2000/ORATOS Data Access (SoDA) software. The tracking data are ESA IFMS ranging, Doppler, meteo and AGC files fetched through the NIS (see [NCTRS/NIS](../scos2000/nctrs-nis.md)) and stored in the FARC, plus NASA/DSN ODF and media calibration files obtained via the RACSO gateway. From the FDS to the MCS go auxiliary data files for experimenters (orbit, attitude, events, comet models, FORTRAN access software), command request files (FDR for the scheduler, DOR for the manual stack), trajectory data (STDMs for ESA stations, CCSDS Orbit Data Message EPMs for the DSN), the interplanetary WIMPY and the One-Way Light Time file used by MCS [time correlation](../scos2000/time-correlation.md).

All file exchanges except Rosetta MPTS files use the MCS File Transfer System (FTS) with the naming convention `TTTT_SSSDDD_t<14 chars>_vvvvv.ROS|MEX`. The document lists high-priority operational files, the manual SFTP procedure across the RACSO/OSCAR security boundary, node addresses, and complete per-mission file-type tables. Section 7.7 is valuable for [MIB tailoring](../mib/tailoring.md): `ccf.dat` gains a 40-character description and a `CCF_SUBSCH` on-board sub-schedule field, and `pcf.dat` gains a 24-character description and the fields `PCF_WDLEN`, `PCF_GRPID`, `PCF_OFFSET` and `PCF_GLOBAL` used to build [PUS service 3](../ecss/pus/st03-housekeeping.md) telecommands. The section also lists the utility hash files that map source-database names to SPIDs and calibration numbers.

key_points.text: Change record: Draft A0 (15/05/99), Draft A1 (31/03/00), Issue A0 (28/03/01) and Draft B0 (07/02/03, DCRs 173 to 207); the title page says Issue B1, 2003-03-07.

The MCS converts packet definitions extracted from the Source Database into MIB files; packetised data (TM source packets, TC history packets (TBC), time coefficient history packets) are extracted from the DAS by FDS using SoDA.

ESA tracking data files are stored on the IFMS at the ESA stations; the MCS obtains them via the Network Interface Subsystem (NIS) and stores them in the MCS FARC. NASA/DSN tracking files come from the FD computer RACSO.

FD command request files are Flight Dynamics Requests (FDR), used by the MCS scheduler subsystem, and Direct Operations Requests (DOR), used by the TC subsystem manual stack; their format is in the CRID.
STDMs for ESA tracking go from FDS to the MCS, are archived in the DAS and pass via the NIS to the station computer; EPMs (CCSDS 502) for NASA/DSN go via RACSO to JPL.
FDS supplies a propagation-delay routine that uses One-Way Light Time (OWLT) files per ground station; the FD ground station ID does not correspond to the NCTRS ground station ID.
All MCS-FDS file transfer except Rosetta MPTS files uses the File Transfer System (FTS); the only delivery acknowledgement is the FTS log, and FTS version numbers wrap from 99999 to 00000.
The FTS is point-to-point: a file needed at two destinations (e.g. NIA and NIB) must be injected twice with different destination codes in its name.
RMCS, MEMCS and FDS all run on SUN/Solaris with 100 Mbps network connections; node names include ROMCA/ROMCB, RONCTRA/RONCTRB, MEMCA/MEMCB, MENCTRA/MENCTRB and RACSO (gateway to OSCAR at JPL).
FTS file naming: TTTT_SSSDDD_txxxxxxxxxxxxxx_vvvvv.yyy (type, source, destination, 'D', 14-character free text, version, ROS or MEX), all upper case; external files are encapsulated with 'tar c'.
The SODA server extracts source packets and SCOS header information through the SCOS-2000 FDIF interface; ORATOS client processes pass packets to the Generic Telemetry Processor (GTP).
MIB tailoring: ccf.dat CCF_DESCR is enlarged from 24 to 40 characters and a new CCF_SUBSCH field (Number(3)) identifies the on-board sub-schedule.

MIB tailoring: pcf.dat PCF_DESCR is enlarged from 16 to 24 characters and PCF_WDLEN ('O' 8-bit or 'W' 16-bit), PCF_GRPID, PCF_OFFSET and PCF_GLOBAL ('G' global or 'D' detailed) are added to build service 3 telecommands; only global parameters are named in service 3 TCs.

The MIB tar file includes utility files spid_hash.txt (RSDB packet name to SPID), calib_hash.txt (RSDB calibration name to calibration number), synparhash.txt (auto-generated synthetic parameter expressions) and list_of_packet_types_not_in_vpd.txt.

notes: The file name (MEX_ESC_ID_5003_FDSICD.PDF, from the Mars Express radio-science archive in the PSA) suggests a Mars Express document ID, but the title page prints RO-ESC-ID-5003, a joint Rosetta/Mars Express ICD. The title page says Issue B1 while the change record stops at Draft B0, and section 1.4 still calls it a draft. Margin change-bar DCR numbers leak into the extracted text, for example '090' next to headings. The 'authors' list gives the people on the approval page (A. Ercolani is listed as Rosetta Technical Officer, preparation by Anite Systems GmbH), not necessarily the writers. The IFMS-OCC reference spells the company 'MakulaMedia' (library item ifms-occ-icd-mex is a later issue, 11.4.0). Section 7.5 cites [S2K-TM-ICD] and section 7.7 cites [S2K-DATABASE-ICD]; neither label is in the reference lists, which have [S2K-PKT-ICD] and [S2K-MIB-ICD] instead. One node address is printed as 'rdsa.ops.esoc.esa.det' (typo). Comet and asteroid names appear as 'Otawara'/'Otwara', 'Siwa' and 'Wirtanen' (original Rosetta targets). Page 6 of the PDF is blank.
